name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index near 104.0 on 25 Nov, 4.3% higher over three months, back inside the 5% line
state: The DXY dollar index was near 104.0 early on 25 Nov, close to its 52-week high of 104.3 but 4.3% higher over three months, back inside the 5% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). The level is inside the 90–108 range, and SOFR stayed within 2bp of the Fed's reserve rate in the five days to 23 Nov (FRED), so no dollar funding stress is visible. The measured data now rate it Normal.
for_you: A strong dollar raises the cost of dollar-priced imports such as oil for other countries and of dollar debt for emerging economies. It is near a one-year high.
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
